methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-institution cohort (National Cancer Institute of Milan, 2016-2023) of 253 SGC patients with centralized histopathologic review and standardized IHC/FISH/NGS assays, which is a strength given disease rarity. Weaknesses include the retrospective nature, heterogeneous molecular testing (panels evolved from <=50 genes to CGP), inability to classify HA AdCC by solid component, and minimal statistical hypothesis testing (only descriptive statistics and a reverse Kaplan-Meier follow-up). No sensitivity analyses or validation cohort are presented, and denominators vary across analyses depending on panel availability.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective single-center case series of consecutive SGC patients, mapping to Oxford LoE 4. The proposed histology-driven stepwise algorithm (MYB/MYBL1 FISH in AdCC; HER2 and AR IHC first in HA non-AdCC; ETV6-NTRK3 FISH in LA non-AdCC) has direct implications for optimizing molecular testing in a rare-tumor setting with limited systemic therapy options and provides cost estimates (~63 euro IHC vs 1550-2070 euro NGS) that could influence practice in resource-constrained settings.

reporting_quality.justification: The cohort is a retrospective observational study and would fall under STROBE; the manuscript is not explicitly flagged as STROBE-compliant, but it reports eligibility, data sources, variables, and limitations adequately. Detailed assay protocols, variant classification criteria (ACMG-based categories, ESCAT), and cohort flow are documented. Data availability is limited: supplementary tables are referenced with redacted URLs and there is no repository deposition; individual-level molecular data are not shared.

novelty_literature.justification: The underlying molecular findings in SGCs (MYB/MYBL1 fusions in AdCC, HER2/AR in SDC, ETV6-NTRK3 in secretory carcinoma) are well described in prior literature cited by the authors (Ross et al. 2017; Skalova 2010; Dalin 2017). The novel contribution is integrating histology, IHC, FISH, and NGS into a single cost-conscious, stepwise algorithm with explicit STOP/GO decision points and a HER2-low subgroup analysis. This is a meaningful synthesis rather than a discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with an IMRaD structure, informative oncoplots (Fig 1), HER2/AR cross-tabulations (Fig 2), and a practical algorithm diagram (Fig 3). Abstract bullet summaries and concrete cost figures aid clinician uptake. Some descriptions contain typographical issues (e.g., 'prevelence' in Table 3) and heavy reliance on supplementary tables for key denominators slightly affects flow.

key_strengths: Largest single-institution SGC MP cohort (n=253) with centralized histopathology review
Practical, cost-conscious, stepwise histology-driven MP algorithm with explicit STOP/GO logic
Integrates IHC/FISH and NGS across AdCC, HA non-AdCC (HER2/AR), and LA non-AdCC
HER2-low subgroup analysis adds novel granularity relevant to emerging anti-HER2 ADCs
key_concerns: Retrospective design with heterogeneous NGS panels evolving across 2016-2023, creating variable denominators
HA AdCC (>=30% solid component) could not be classified, limiting algorithm completeness for AdCC
Only 4% (11/253) actually received MP-guided therapy, limiting outcome inferences
Minimal inferential statistics; no validation cohort or external replication
No individual-level data deposition; supplementary URLs redacted in this version
chief_reviewer.rationale: Pragmatic, well-organized descriptive study in a rare-cancer context whose main contribution is an actionable histology-driven testing algorithm; the retrospective design, heterogeneous assays, and absence of validation cap its ceiling at tier 3 with minor revisions.
